channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: New Hospital and Health Center Opened in Shamsiddin Shohin District, Tajikistan
item.description: A new Central Hospital and health center opened on October 6, 2026, in Tajikistan's Shamsiddin Shohin district. Built with Asian Development Bank support, the hospital has 66 beds and modern equipment. The project also included a new 53-bed hospital building and a health center.

item.title: Kazakhstan Lawmaker Highlights Critical Drug Accessibility Issues
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai deputy, Askhat Aimagambetov, raised concerns about the availability of essential modern medicines. He cited a case where a prescribed drug was unavailable locally, costing significantly more abroad or requiring purchase of excess quantities.

item.title: Moscow to Host Regional Security Talks on Afghanistan and Central Asia
item.description: Moscow will host a regional security meeting on October 15-16, focusing on Afghanistan and Central Asia. Representatives from CSTO, CIS, and SCO will discuss security developments and emerging challenges. A separate CSTO Collective Security Council meeting is scheduled for November 10-11 to strengthen collective security and cooperation.

item.title: CSTO Announces Security Meeting on Afghanistan and Central Asia in Moscow
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) announced a joint meeting on security in Central Asia and Afghanistan will be held in Moscow on October 15-16. The meeting, involving CSTO, CIS, and SCO, aims to expand security cooperation. A CSTO Collective Security Council meeting is scheduled for November 10-11 to adopt decisions strengthening the alliance's collective security system.

item.title: Former Minister Sues Ex-Editor Demanding Retraction and Professionalism Claims
item.description: A civil court in Almaty has begun hearing a lawsuit filed by former Education Minister Gani Beisembayev against Gulnara Bazhenova, ex-editor of Orda.kz. The former minister seeks a retraction of alleged 'family ties' to Murat Nurtleu, 20 million tenge in moral damages, and legal costs. The court session is proceeding online.

item.title: Almaty Architects Urge Prime Minister Not to Approve General Plan Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Materials from an investigation into public discussions of Almaty's general plan have been sent to the National Security Committee (KNB). The Almaty Union of Architects' consultative commission urged the Prime Minister not to approve the plan, citing irregularities in the public consultation process and the handling of voting records.

item.title: Child Dies in Mangystau After Suspected Fish Poisoning; Medical Help Sought Three Days Later
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health commented on the death of a child in the Mangystau region following suspected poisoning from smoked fish. The ministry stated that by the time medical help was sought, the child's condition was critical, three days after consuming the fish. Despite intensive care and consultations with national specialists, the child died on October 6 due to irreversible complications.

item.title: Law Exists, But Medicines Are Unavailable: Deputy Aimagambetov Concerned Over High Drug Prices
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Askhat Aimagambetov highlighted the issue of inaccessible modern medications in Kazakhstan, despite legislative improvements. He cited a case where a 14-day course of a drug, costing approximately 11,000 tenge in Japan, was unavailable in Kazakhstan. Resellers offered the medication for nearly half a million tenge, making treatment unaffordable for patients.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Attends Central Asia and Azerbaijan Leaders Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Turkmenbashi to participate in the 8th Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan. The summit includes leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Azerbaijan. President Serdar Berdimuhamedov of Turkmenistan welcomed the Kazakh leader.

item.title: France in Talks with Taliban on Deporting Afghan Nationals
item.description: France has initiated talks with the Taliban's Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (IEA) to facilitate the deportation of Afghan nationals from France. A diplomatic source stated these discussions are technical and aim to remove individuals without legal status deemed a threat to public order. This does not signify a change in France's overall stance on Afghanistan.

item.title: World Financial Review Analyzes Kazakhstan's Shifting Investment Landscape
item.description: The World Financial Review highlights Kazakhstan's progress in diversifying its economy beyond raw materials. The publication notes the country's transformation into Central Asia's largest economy, with GDP per capita exceeding $15,000. It also mentions significant foreign investment inflows and positive growth forecasts from international financial institutions like the EBRD and ADB.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens 72 Criminal Cases for Inciting Interethnic Strife Online
item.description: Kazakhstan has initiated 72 criminal cases related to inciting social, national, ethnic, racial, or religious discord over the past nine months. Additionally, 64 cases were opened for spreading false information, with 124 individuals held accountable for posting illegal content online. Authorities are developing a monitoring system for open sources.

item.title: Anti-War Orthodox Priest Sentenced to Four Years on Drug Charges in Almaty
item.description: A former Russian Orthodox priest, Father Iakov Vorontsov, has been sentenced to four years in prison in Almaty, Kazakhstan, on drug charges. He was found guilty of illegally acquiring and possessing a banned synthetic psychotropic substance. His sentence was reduced due to a national amnesty law.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Agree on Water Volume for Sardara Reservoir
item.description: The 95th meeting of the Interstate Coordination Water Commission of Central Asian states was held in Turkmenbashi. Representatives from Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan finalized water intake limits and reservoir operation plans for the 2026-2027 inter-vegetation period. The Sardara reservoir received 3.69 billion cubic meters of water, exceeding projections by 840 million cubic meters.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Needs-Based Social Benefits from 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan will implement a needs-based system for social benefits starting January 1, 2027. A government decree signed by Prime Minister Oljas Bektenov outlines criteria for eligibility, suspension, and resumption of payments. This includes benefits for childbirth, childcare, large families, disability, and loss of a breadwinner, assessed based on family's social well-being.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Generous Childbirth Support System Exceeds Regional Averages
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a comprehensive family support system, allocating approximately 27% of its 2026 republican budget to social protection, comparable to OECD nations. Lump-sum payments for newborns vary, with the fourth child receiving a higher amount. These benefits are significantly more substantial than those in neighboring Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kazakh citizens allegedly lured into Russian army service and sent to war
item.description: Relatives of Kazakh citizens claim at least 21 individuals were deceived into serving in the Russian army and sent to the war zone. They allege young men seeking work in Russia were pressured into signing contracts and deployed to combat areas. Kazakhstan's MFA is investigating and coordinating with Russian authorities.

item.title: Two Workers Die from Gas Poisoning in Shymkent
item.description: Two workers replacing a water pipeline in Shymkent died from gas poisoning. The men, aged 20-22, entered a well and lost consciousness. Colleagues found them, but two could not be saved. The third worker received medical attention and was sent home. An investigation into labor safety is underway.

item.title: Residents of New Housing in Ridder Complain of Poor Construction Quality
item.description: Residents of new homes built under the 'One-Story East' program in Ridder, Kazakhstan, are complaining about poor construction quality. They report cold floors, dampness, mold, and drafts. The akimat purchased the homes from private developers and claims no significant issues were found during construction.

item.title: Afghan National Resistance Front Denies Taliban Allegations of Attack Plot
item.description: The National Resistance Front of Afghanistan has rejected a Taliban video claiming a plot to attack UNAMA in Kabul, calling the featured confessions "coerced." The front described the video as a "forced narrative" and disinformation, urging international institutions to investigate its production and the circumstances of the confessions.

item.title: Shopkeeper Murdered in Laghman by Taliban Intelligence Officer
item.description: Local sources in Laghman report that a shopkeeper named Afghan Kakker was killed in Mehtarlam city by a member of the Taliban's intelligence directorate. The Taliban member reportedly shot the shopkeeper after a verbal dispute. The perpetrator's identity is known, but local Taliban officials have not commented on any arrest or investigation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Abolishes Norms Allowing Acceptance of Defective Roads
item.description: Kazakhstan has abolished norms that permitted the acceptance of road construction projects with unrectified defects. The Chief Transport Prosecutor's Office found that the methodology allowed for project acceptance even if surface deficiencies were not fixed, with financial penalties instead of repairs. Provisions allowing acceptance of work with unaddressed defects have been removed from the Ministry of Transport's order.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Manufacturing Sector Surpasses Extractive Industries, Reports British Publication
item.description: Kazakhstan's manufacturing industry has overtaken its extractive sector, indicating a reduced reliance on raw materials, according to The World Financial Review. Over the past seven years, 625 industrial enterprises were established, creating nearly 62,000 jobs. Automotive manufacturing and agriculture have seen significant growth, alongside an increase in small and medium-sized businesses and housing construction.

item.title: US Military Preparing for Potential Strikes Against Iran, Axios Reports
item.description: The US military is preparing to resume major combat operations against Iran, according to Axios, citing US officials. The potential strikes could occur before the November midterm elections. The Pentagon has ordered CENTCOM to finalize preparations, though a specific start date has not been set. Targets may include Iran's energy, infrastructure, and nuclear facilities.

item.title: Ancient Turkic Khaganate Settlement Discovered in East Kazakhstan Region
item.description: Archaeologists have discovered a large settlement, believed to date back to the 6th-7th centuries AD, in the Zaisan basin of the East Kazakhstan region. The site, spanning over 25 hectares, shows preserved internal structures and artifacts. Preliminary analysis suggests a connection to the First Turkic Khaganate period.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Dollar Exchange Rate Forecasted for Early November
item.description: Market experts predict the dollar exchange rate in Kazakhstan to be around 456.5 tenge by early November, down from 474.2 tenge a month prior. The national currency is supported by high yields, an improved sovereign rating, National Bank sales, and foreign investment.

item.title: Debate on Pedophilia Punishment: Experts Discuss Castration, Life Imprisonment, and Death Penalty
item.description: Following a child sexual assault case, Uzbekistan is revisiting punishments for pedophilia. Experts like lawyer Kamola Aliyeva argue that castration, life imprisonment, or the death penalty are not effective solutions. She highlights that chemical castration is reversible and voluntary, making it unsuitable for Uzbekistan's context.

item.title: Kazakhstan Experiences Widespread Internet Outage on "TransTelekom" Network
item.description: A significant internet disruption affected all of Kazakhstan starting late on October 8th, impacting users of the "TransTelekom" communication operator. The company confirmed the issue, which caused slow or complete loss of connectivity. Technical specialists worked to restore services, and full restoration was announced later that day.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Uncovers Flaw in Road Quality Acceptance Process
item.description: Kazakhstan's Main Transport Prosecutor's Office has identified a loophole in the National Center for Road Quality Assets' methodology. The current procedure allows for the acceptance of road construction works with defects, without proper restoration of road surface characteristics. Instead of fixing issues, financial penalties or extended warranty periods were applied.

item.title: Khujand Completes Autumn Conscription Plan Ahead of Schedule
item.description: The autumn conscription plan for military service in Tajikistan's Armed Forces in Khujand has been fulfilled 100% in the initial days of the campaign. City authorities attribute this early completion to the efforts of city leadership, the military commissariat, mahalla chairmen, and parental responsibility. Some conscripts received free driver's licenses after attending driving school.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Remain Among Fastest-Growing Economies in Europe and Central Asia in 2026 - World Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan is projected to remain among the fastest-growing economies in Europe and Central Asia in 2026, with real GDP growth expected to accelerate to 7.9%, the highest forecast in the region. Economic growth is driven by stable domestic demand, rising real wages, increased employment, higher remittances, and ongoing structural reforms.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Initiatives Aim for Economic Results in Central Asia and Azerbaijan
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the 8th Consultative Meeting of Central Asian Heads of State and Azerbaijan, and the CIS Heads of State Council meeting. Initiated by Uzbekistan in 2017, these meetings address transit, infrastructure, border procedures, and production cooperation. Azerbaijan's full participation enhances coordination for Central Asian development with South Caucasus transport routes.

item.title: Pakistan PM and Army Chief Discuss Security Concerns, Terrorism from Afghanistan with UN Chief
item.description: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Syed Asim Munir met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres to express serious concerns over terrorism originating from Afghanistan. Sharif stressed the need for concrete action against groups Islamabad alleges operate from Afghan territory, while Afghan officials deny these claims.

item.title: Freedom Front claims rocket attack on Taliban outposts in Kapisa
item.description: The Freedom Front reported conducting rocket and gunfire attacks on Taliban outposts in Kapisa province early Wednesday morning. The group claimed at least three Taliban members were killed and two wounded during the 20-minute engagement in the Poza-e Khamzargar area. This follows recent clashes reported in Nuristan province.

item.title: Kabul residents face hefty service fees and rent demands from Taliban
item.description: Residents of Omar Gulistan town in Kabul are reportedly being charged 2,000 Afghanis monthly for 'service fees' and 5,000 Afghanis per room as 'rent' by the Taliban. This comes after the Taliban declared the town 'Emirati' and claimed ownership of the land, despite residents losing their property rights.

item.title: Tashkent Technical University Evicts 300 Students from Uncommissioned Dormitory
item.description: Around 300 students were evicted from a new dormitory at Tashkent Technical University. The Ministry of Higher Education stated the dormitory was not officially commissioned, lacked permits, and had incomplete heating and hot water systems. The entrepreneur who housed students before commissioning is reportedly responsible.

item.title: National Resistance Front Denies Taliban Claims of Arrests and Attack Plot
item.description: The National Resistance Front of Afghanistan has denied the Taliban's claims of arresting its members and plotting an attack against UNAMA. The group stated the Taliban's allegations are fabricated propaganda intended to justify attacks by the Taliban themselves against foreign entities. They warned foreign organizations in Afghanistan to increase security measures.

item.title: Tashkent Needs Nearly 1000 Hectares of Green Space to Match Almaty Standards
item.description: Tashkent requires approximately 1000 hectares of additional large green and forest-park areas to approach Almaty's level of greening, according to Tashkent Mayor Shavkat Umurzakov. He stated that by 2035-2040, the city aims to create about 3000 hectares of green space within its current boundaries, excluding the new city project.

item.title: United Front Claims Taliban Fighter Killed in Ghor Province Attack
item.description: The United Front of Afghanistan reported an attack on a Taliban outpost in the Pasaband district of Ghor province, claiming one fighter was killed and another wounded. This incident follows recent guerrilla operations by the United Front against the Taliban in Kandahar and Helmand provinces.

item.title: Tajikistan Approves Amendments to Convention on International Civil Aviation
item.description: Tajikistan's lower house of parliament has approved amendments to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, specifically Articles 50(a) and 56. The changes, signed in 2016, aim to improve the ICAO's governance structure and increase member state representation by expanding the Council from 36 to 40 states.
